intervals.label: operation
intervals.note: Start is the founding of the Institute by intergovernmental agreement; the ILL pages consulted do not date the reactor's first operation. Still operating as of verified_at (the ILL reactor overview describes the reactor running in cycles of about 60 days).
intervals.quote: The ILL was founded on 19 January 1967 with the signing of an agreement between the governments of the French Republic and the Federal Republic of Germany.

name: Institut Laue-Langevin
notes: Host facility of the Ricochet experiment.

ILL is primarily a multinational neutron-science user facility; it is recorded here as a reactor site because the property relevant to Ricochet's CEvNS program is its 58 MW (thermal) research reactor core, as for the other CEvNS reactor facilities (Brokdorf, Leibstadt).

operator.note: The Institute is its own operator; its own page names the three funding and managing countries.
operator.quote: Funded and managed by France, Germany and the United Kingdom, and in scientific partnership with 10 other countries, ILL is located in a dynamic and scientifically rich city of Grenoble
operator.value: Institut Laue-Langevin (an international research centre funded and managed by France, Germany and the United Kingdom)

summary.plain: A major research reactor in Grenoble, France, mainly used to make beams of neutrons for science, and also home to the Ricochet reactor-neutrino experiment.
summary.technical: Institut Laue-Langevin (ILL), Grenoble, France: research reactor of 58 MW thermal power (ILL's own reactor page; Ricochet's own background paper also gives 58 MW); hosts the Ricochet CEvNS experiment 8.8 m from the reactor core.
